confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web search summaries, not on venue menus that I read directly. Restaurant meals, coffee and beer come from Numbeo's Lima figures (updated mid-November 2026, in soles): about S/17.4 for an inexpensive meal, S/120 for a mid-range meal for two, S/11 for a cappuccino and S/10.2 for a domestic draft beer. Other summaries (HikersBay, Wise, WhereAndWhen) roughly agree. I converted soles to US dollars at about 3.4 PEN per USD, which comes from the PEN and USD pairs in the HikersBay and Expatistan snippets. It is not an official PEN rate. The cocktail is the least certain drink: a Portuguese-language guide gave a citywide range of S/18-35 for a pisco sour, using April 2025 prices, and I took a value near the middle. I found no aggregated price for a glass of wine. That estimate comes from Expatistan's retail bottle price (about S/49, or USD 15), a normal restaurant markup, and its usual relationship to the beer and cocktail prices. All accommodation anchors are my own general-knowledge estimates for areas tourists use, such as Miraflores and Barranco, in July 2026. I did not search for them or check any listings. July is Lima's cool, grey season, but rooms may cost more around the late-July national holidays (Fiestas Patrias). The RBA rate of 0.6720 USD per AUD on 18 November 2026 comes from a search result summary that named the RBA's 4pm fixing. A secondary aggregator (ozfinancehub) showed the same figure. I did not open the RBA page itself, so the server should check the value against the official RBA feed.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Numbeo's citywide Lima figures for restaurant, coffee and beer prices. For accommodation, I used other large South American capitals as the regional basis, mainly Bogotá and Santiago. Lima's tourist districts (Miraflores and Barranco) cost a little less than Santiago and about the same as or a little more than Bogotá.
